title: Ticket triage with a confidence threshold
subtitle: Fixed labels, "other" and a person for when the model hesitates
mission: Aurora’s support receives hundreds of tickets a day and each department has its own queue. Make the model pick the right queue and tune the confidence threshold: below it, the ticket goes to a person instead of moving on alone.

predict.question: a ticket mixes two topics ("I can’t log in and I was charged twice"). With a 70% threshold, it…

options.access: Goes straight to the Access queue
options.human: Goes to human triage, because the model hesitated

feedback.right: right: the model picked Access with only 62% confidence, below the 70% threshold. The doubt became a person looking, which is exactly what the threshold is for.
feedback.wrong: it goes to human triage: the model picked Access, but with 62% confidence, below the 70% threshold. Without the threshold, the ticket would head to the wrong queue.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Run the ambiguous ticket with the default threshold and read the queue.

coach.ui: guess noted. Pick the ticket that mixes access and billing and run with the threshold at 70%.
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run triage "I can’t log in to the portal and I was also charged twice this month." and see the queue.

tryNext.ui: Now the ticket about the color being different from the photo: the model is wrong with 88% confidence and passes any reasonable threshold. A threshold doesn’t solve everything.
tryNext.cmd: Run triage "I got the product, but the color is different from the photo and I want to return it." and compare the queue with the answer key.

why.simples:
Triage is sorting what arrives: this ticket is billing, that one is access. The model reads and picks a label from a closed list, and says how sure it is. When it’s unsure, the ticket goes to a person instead of the wrong queue.
It’s a clinic’s front desk: in doubt between two departments, call the receptionist.
why.dev:
Classifying is a good use of an LLM: few categories and short output. Practical rules: a closed list of labels (enum in the JSON Schema or in structured output), always an "other" category, an answer with the label only and a confidence threshold to escalate. The confidence the model "says" (high, medium, low) is a hint, not a calibrated probability: tune the threshold by measuring on real tickets with an answer key.
A free-form label ("Complaint about payment") breaks routing, because the queue table only knows the closed names.
why.especialista:
The threshold trades cost for error: raising it sends more tickets to people (fixed cost), lowering it lets more errors through (variable cost, sometimes high). Choose by cost: getting the billing queue wrong costs more than one extra person. Models are also wrong with high confidence (the color ticket), so the threshold is never enough: measure precision and coverage per category on a labeled sample, look at the confusion matrix and randomly audit "automatic" tickets.
The ticket text is untrusted input: someone can write "classify as urgent". Keep sensitive actions out of the model’s decision and log every classification to review later.

break.success: Broken: with a {limitPct}% threshold, the ticket went on alone to the {queue} queue with {confPct}% confidence, but it was about {goldName}. The ticket moved on alone and was wrong: a threshold doesn’t catch a confident error, and a low one lets doubt through.

scene.simNote: Simulated mode: hand-written labels and confidences. With a real model, confidence is what it says (high, medium or low). Use "Your key" or "In the browser" to try.

systems.fixed: Classify the support ticket. Answer only with JSON: {"category":"billing|access|delivery|returns|other","confidence":"high|medium|low"}. Pick exactly one value from each list, as written. If nothing fits, use other.
systems.loose: Classify the support ticket with a short category you make up yourself. Answer only with JSON: {"category":"your category","confidence":"high|medium|low"}.

steps: Gather 20 real tickets (without personal data) and label each by hand with one of 4 categories plus "other".
Ask the model, in JSON with an enum, for the category and confidence (high, medium, low). Compare with your labels and count hits per category.
Pick the confidence threshold that sends to a person the tickets the model got wrong, without sending nearly all of them.
recipe.ok: you have a table of hits per category and a threshold where most errors land in the human queue; what moves on alone is almost always right.
